# Topics

> Understand how a Topic keeps shared work, decisions, and their completion in one place.

A Topic is a lasting place for a piece of work that people or agents need to follow together. It keeps the intent, conversation, relevant context, and progress tied to one identity, even when the work pauses or the conversation continues later. Use a Topic when there is something to deliver, answer, decide, review, or revisit.

## A Kind gives the work a purpose

Every Topic has a **Kind** that describes the job it does. A Task coordinates work; a Project coordinates milestones and related work. A Question seeks an answer, while an Evaluation assesses evidence or options against criteria. A Proposal puts something forward for approval. Discussion, Claims, Incident, and Agent Task Kinds serve different jobs. An Agent Task commissions bounded agent work; it is not every Task that an agent helps with.

The Kind gives the Topic a starting structure. People can also choose a reusable Topic Recipe when one is available. A recipe can suggest how to organise the work, but it does not assign people, grant permissions, or perform actions on its own.

## A draft makes the intent reviewable

Every new Topic starts as a draft. Its setup can describe the purpose, the intended outcome, the scope, who will do the work, and who can accept the result. People review and confirm the setup before it becomes effective. If a required person or decision is still unknown, the draft keeps that gap visible instead of assuming an answer.

Confirming the setup allows the Topic to progress. It does not mean that someone has agreed to a contract, accepted an outcome, approved an action, or completed the Topic. Those steps have their own requirements.

## Progress is separate from completion

A Topic can carry records of work, evidence, decisions, and results. Its progress shows what still needs attention and who is responsible for the next step. A finished task, a successful action, an approved outcome, or a payment can contribute to that record without automatically completing the Topic. Completion follows the Topic's defined completion step.

## Shared context has boundaries

A Topic's conversation lives within an IXO Matrix room. The room determines who can see that conversation, so a smaller confidential audience needs a separate room. A Topic can refer to a file, claim, or other resource without giving room members access to that resource.

Being the creator, owner, or a room member does not by itself authorize someone to edit setup, approve a result, or take an external action. Each consequential step needs the relevant permission and authority. This lets people share context while keeping decisions and effects accountable.

For the wider cooperation model, read [Qi Intelligent Cooperating System](/articles/qi-intelligent-cooperating-system). For the room boundary, read [IXO Matrix](/articles/ixo-matrix).
